solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Coping with supporters a bad result upset?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether coping with their backers through a disappointing outcome is upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coping' looks like dealing with something, but it is the capping course on top of a wall, here resting on supporting posts.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a rail or coping held up by a row of small pillars, the supporters.

clue.text: Lure one inside club

indicators.note: inside says the numeral piece sits within the word for the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tempting offer is placed inside a nightclub to draw people in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a lure is a temptation set to draw prey or a person in.

clue.text: Grating in top room secured by the Parisian

indicators.note: secured by means held between, so the French article goes round the room word

parts.note: le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it
an attic is the room at the top of a house

explanation.surface: A grating in a Paris attic is held fast by the landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a grating is a framework of crossed bars, the same as a criss-cross lattice.

clue.text: Conference on top of Snowdon, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a meeting of heads of government or leaders
read literally, a gathering held at the peak of a mountain such as Snowdon

explanation.walkthrough: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales; a meeting on its peak would literally be held at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of heads of state is called a top-level summit, hence the phrase for such a conference.

clue.text: Artist's short name for a villain

parts.note: RA (Royal Academician) is the usual abbreviation for an artist, with the possessive S

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back, losing its final letter

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A painter's abbreviated nickname for the bad guy in his picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue or scoundrel, a mild villain, is a common meaning of this word.

clue.text: Private eye probing exploit is thorough

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so the detective word goes into the middle of the feat word

parts.note: an exploit is a deed or feat
a tail is someone who follows a suspect, a private detective

explanation.surface: A detective investigating some escapade is being diligent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private eye' suggests PI or DET, but here it is the person who follows a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a thorough account covers every particular, which is what a minute, itemised report does.

clue.text: Insect beginning to wound snake

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: an asp is a small venomous snake

explanation.surface: An insect starts to injure a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this striped stinging insect is one kind of insect.

clue.text: One flies from Scandinavia to Russia

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone who makes the trip by air between the Nordic countries and Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is one who flies an aircraft, the plain meaning of the word.

clue.text: Extremely popular English artist on a great deal? More or less

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters, of the next word

parts.note: William Etty was an English painter of the 19th century
much means a great deal

explanation.surface: Asks whether a very popular English painter is roughly a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for popular, but it takes that word's outer letters, P and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an idiom for nearly or approximately, much like saying almost.

clue.text: Narrow strip of land is therefore blocked by leader of militia

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: blocked by means the next letter is lodged inside the word for therefore

parts.note: thus means therefore

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of militia

explanation.surface: A thin neck of land is therefore cut off by a militia commander.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a thin neck of land joining two larger landmasses, such as Panama.

clue.text: New 2, pleasant to touch

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of the referenced answer are reformed

parts.note: refers to the answer to 2 down, the word for grating

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: a new version of 2 down is nice to feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' takes the letters of the 2 down answer (the grating) and rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to touch: the word describes the sense of feeling, so something tactual or pleasant to handle.

clue.text: Seeing fit Conservative on the way down

parts.note: descending means going down

explanation.surface: A Tory deciding something is appropriate while his party heads downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to deign, to see fit to do something beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: French filmmaker in sight making tour of inspection

indicators.note: in places the filmmaker's name inside the word for sight

parts.note: vision is sight
Jacques Tati was a French film director and comedian

explanation.surface: A French director comes into view while making an official round.
explanation.definitionFit: An official visit to inspect, such as a bishop's survey of a diocese, is this word.

clue.text: Perfect without a toddler?

indicators.note: without means leaving out the following word's letter

parts.note: to a T means perfectly, exactly right

explanation.surface: Asks whether perfection is possible without a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'to a T' (perfectly) loses its A, leaving TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a tot is a small child, one just learning to walk.

clue.text: Use The Oaks, flourishing restaurant

indicators.note: flourishing means waving about with a flourish, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to go to The Oaks, a thriving place to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a restaurant that specialises in grilled beef is this kind of eatery.

clue.text: Louise's partner playing Hamlet

indicators.note: playing means acting out, so the play's title letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Louise's companion is on stage as the Prince of Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: Thelma & Louise is a 1991 film about two women on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: In the road movie the two heroines are a pair, so Louise's friend and companion is this woman.

clue.text: Message spread caused upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue would mean turned over; here it signals that the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: marge is short for margarine, a spread
let means caused or allowed, as in let it be known

explanation.surface: News spread around and caused distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses MARGE + LET (MARGELET) to give the message.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a wire sent and delivered on paper was a kind of message.

clue.text: Beggar born on barge

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for born, as in biographies
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for carrying goods

explanation.surface: A vagrant was born aboard a canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beggar' here is the British jokey insult, as in 'you lucky beggar', not a person asking for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a fellow or wretch, a mildly abusive name for a person.

clue.text: Notably, a black smock Romeo discarded

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so the letter for Romeo is dropped

parts.note: an overall is a loose protective smock
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Pointedly, Romeo threw off a dark work smock.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: particularly or especially, as in most importantly of everything else.

clue.text: Where hands may be seen doing lookout duty

definitions.meaning: the hour and minute hands are found on a timepiece
a sentry or sailor keeping guard during a set shift

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' suggests crew members, but the first reading is the hands of a clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the position of clock hands, and idiomatically being on guard during a shift.

clue.text: Very famous figure in charge

parts.note: an icon is an image or figure

explanation.surface: A celebrated person takes the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something widely recognised as a symbol is renowned and celebrated.

clue.text: Very good French resort, on top of everything

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter, the head of everything in a down light

explanation.surface: A French seaside town that tops everything.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom of praise, an exclamation meaning well done or excellent.

clue.text: Medical Officer on barge in capital

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed barge

explanation.surface: A doctor travelling by barge into the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Russian capital city.

clue.text: Cut down cast in the auditorium

indicators.note: in the auditorium means as heard by an audience, so a word sounding the same is meant

parts.note: a cast is a tinge or shade of colour, a hue

explanation.surface: Actors trimmed in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors, but here it is a tint of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to fell a tree with an axe or chop it down.

clue.text: Well cared for, serving time here?

definitions.meaning: a prisoner serving a sentence would be in jail, and nick is slang for prison

explanation.walkthrough: NICK is British slang for a prison or police station; IN GOOD NICK is British for in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for in fine shape, and literally inside a respectable jail.

clue.text: Song of praise suggested by that man on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means broadcast and heard, so the words are as spoken

parts.note: him refers to that man

explanation.surface: A worship song proposed by a male presenter on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a religious song of worship sung in church.

clue.text: Out of bed, drunk is nervy

parts.note: up means out of bed
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone just risen and inebriated is on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: tense and anxious, on edge.

clue.text: Stylish plant? Fact dismissed in plant

parts.note: chic means stylish

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so the word fact is taken off

parts.note: a plant is a factory or works

explanation.surface: A fashionable plant, then a fact rejected about a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'plant?' is the industrial plant, a works; the second is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a blue-flowered herb whose roots are roasted as a coffee substitute is one kind of plant.

clue.text: Code word used in speech — Oscar

indicators.note: used in means found inside, so letters are taken from within speech

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A radio signaller saying a code word, then Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is the NATO alphabet word for the letter E, a code word.

clue.text: Top Greek and English men heading off for a game of bowls?

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head or a hat

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

explanation.surface: Leading Greek and English men set off to play bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowls is a lawn game of rolling balls towards a small target ball; crown green bowls is a northern English form played on a domed lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A domed lawn laid out for playing bowls is this kind of green.
